notes: 'as for an only son' is read as the construct relation of אֵבֶל יָחִיד recast with a preposition (rule 19), not as rule 16's fronted-object formula; no object marker stands here.

'gird thee' keeps its reflexive pronoun with the verb because the ASV uses it for the middle sense of חָגַר rather than to supply an object, the object being שָׂק; 'wallow thyself' goes the same way for the Hithpael (rule 44).
The dative לְ of עֲשִׂי לָךְ is unrepresented and its suffix takes the bare object 'thee' (rule 40).
